purpose.en: Zootomy is a comparative muscle atlas for dog, cat and horse. Turn the animal with one finger, tap a muscle to read what it does IN THAT SPECIES, and switch species from the tabs — your pick follows you, because the same muscle carries the same id in all three. Every card also gives the human-equivalent name and the one thing that is genuinely different. Schematic model, for learning, not a clinical reference.
purpose.ko: 주토미는 개, 고양이, 말의 근육을 비교하는 아틀라스입니다. 손가락 하나로 동물을 돌리고, 근육을 탭해서 그 종에서 하는 역할을 읽어보세요. 탭에서 종을 바꾸면 선택한 근육이 그대로 따라옵니다 — 세 종 모두 같은 근육에 같은 id를 쓰기 때문입니다. 각 카드는 인간의 대응 명칭과 진짜로 다른 점 한 가지도 알려줍니다. 학습용 개략 모델이며, 임상 참고 자료가 아닙니다.
purpose.zh: Zootomy 是狗、猫和马的比较肌肉图谱。用一根手指旋转动物，点击肌肉查看它在该物种中的作用，并从标签切换物种——你的选择会跟随，因为同一块肌肉在三种动物中共用同一个id。每张卡片还给出对应的人类名称，以及一个真正不同之处。此为示意模型，仅供学习，非临床参考。
purpose.hi: ज़ूटॉमी कुत्ते, बिल्ली और घोड़े के लिए एक तुलनात्मक मांसपेशी एटलस है। एक उंगली से जानवर को घुमाएँ, किसी मांसपेशी को टैप करके जानें कि वह उस प्रजाति में क्या करती है, और टैब से प्रजाति बदलें — आपका चयन आपके साथ रहता है, क्योंकि तीनों में एक ही मांसपेशी की एक ही id होती है। हर कार्ड मानव-समकक्ष नाम और एक वास्तविक अंतर भी बताता है। यह सीखने के लिए एक स्कीमैटिक मॉडल है, नैदानिक संदर्भ नहीं।
purpose.es: Zootomy es un atlas comparativo de músculos de perro, gato y caballo. Gira al animal con un dedo, toca un músculo para leer qué hace EN ESA ESPECIE, y cambia de especie desde las pestañas — tu selección te sigue, porque el mismo músculo lleva el mismo id en las tres. Cada tarjeta también da el nombre equivalente humano y la única diferencia real. Modelo esquemático, para aprender, no una referencia clínica.
purpose.fr: Zootomy est un atlas musculaire comparatif pour le chien, le chat et le cheval. Faites pivoter l'animal d'un doigt, touchez un muscle pour lire son rôle DANS CETTE ESPÈCE, et changez d'espèce depuis les onglets — votre sélection vous suit, car le même muscle porte le même id dans les trois. Chaque fiche donne aussi le nom équivalent humain et la seule chose vraiment différente. Modèle schématique, pour apprendre, pas une référence clinique.
purpose.ar: زوتومي هو أطلس عضلي مقارن للكلب والقط والحصان. أدر الحيوان بإصبع واحد، واضغط على عضلة لقراءة وظيفتها في ذلك النوع، وبدّل الأنواع من علامات التبويب — يظل اختيارك معك لأن نفس العضلة تحمل نفس المعرف في الأنواع الثلاثة. تعطي كل بطاقة أيضًا الاسم المكافئ عند الإنسان والفرق الحقيقي الوحيد. نموذج تخطيطي للتعلم، وليس مرجعًا سريريًا.
purpose.pt: Zootomy é um atlas muscular comparativo de cão, gato e cavalo. Gire o animal com um dedo, toque em um músculo para ler o que ele faz NAQUELA espécie e alterne de espécie pelas abas — sua seleção o acompanha, pois o mesmo músculo tem o mesmo id nas três. Cada cartão também dá o nome equivalente humano e a única diferença real. Modelo esquemático, para aprendizado, não uma referência clínica.
purpose.ru: Zootomy — это сравнительный мышечный атлас для собаки, кошки и лошади. Поворачивайте животное одним пальцем, нажимайте на мышцу, чтобы узнать её функцию именно у ЭТОГО вида, и переключайте вид на вкладках — выбор сохраняется, потому что одна и та же мышца несёт одинаковый id у всех трёх видов. Каждая карточка также даёт название человеческого аналога и единственное по-настоящему отличие. Схематичная модель для обучения, не клинический справочник.
purpose.de: Zootomy ist ein vergleichendes Muskelatlas für Hund, Katze und Pferd. Dreht das Tier mit einem Finger, tippt auf einen Muskel, um zu lesen, was er BEI DIESER ART tut, und wechselt die Art über die Tabs — eure Auswahl bleibt erhalten, weil derselbe Muskel bei allen drei dieselbe id trägt. Jede Karte nennt auch den menschlichen Entsprechungsnamen und den einen wirklich unterschiedlichen Punkt. Schematisches Modell zum Lernen, kein klinisches Nachschlagewerk.
purpose.ja: Zootomyは犬・猫・馬の筋肉を比較するアトラスです。指1本で動物を回転させ、筋肉をタップしてその種における働きを読み、タブで種を切り替えられます — 同じ筋肉は3種すべてで同じidを持つため、選択はそのまま引き継がれます。各カードには対応するヒトの名称と、本当に異なる点も1つ記載されています。学習用の模式モデルであり、臨床上の参考資料ではありません。
purpose.tr: Zootomy, köpek, kedi ve at için karşılaştırmalı bir kas atlasıdır. Hayvanı tek parmakla döndürün, bir kasa dokunarak O TÜRDE ne yaptığını okuyun ve sekmelerden tür değiştirin — seçiminiz sizi takip eder, çünkü aynı kas her üçünde de aynı id'yi taşır. Her kart ayrıca insan karşılığı adını ve gerçekten farklı olan tek şeyi de verir. Öğrenim için şematik model, klinik referans değildir.
purpose.vi: Zootomy là bản đồ cơ so sánh cho chó, mèo và ngựa. Xoay con vật bằng một ngón tay, chạm vào một cơ để đọc chức năng của nó Ở LOÀI ĐÓ, và chuyển loài từ các tab — lựa chọn của bạn vẫn được giữ, vì cùng một cơ mang cùng một id ở cả ba loài. Mỗi thẻ cũng cho biết tên tương đương ở người và một điểm thực sự khác biệt. Mô hình sơ đồ, dùng để học, không phải tài liệu tham khảo lâm sàng.
purpose.it: Zootomy è un atlante muscolare comparativo per cane, gatto e cavallo. Ruota l'animale con un dito, tocca un muscolo per leggere cosa fa IN QUELLA SPECIE, e cambia specie dalle schede — la tua selezione ti segue, perché lo stesso muscolo porta lo stesso id in tutte e tre. Ogni scheda fornisce anche il nome equivalente umano e l'unica vera differenza. Modello schematico, per l'apprendimento, non un riferimento clinico.
purpose.fa: Zootomy یک اطلس عضلانی مقایسه‌ای برای سگ، گربه و اسب است. حیوان را با یک انگشت بچرخانید، روی یک عضله ضربه بزنید تا کارکرد آن را در همان گونه بخوانید، و از تب‌ها گونه را عوض کنید — انتخاب شما دنبال می‌شود، زیرا همان عضله در هر سه گونه همان شناسه را دارد. هر کارت همچنین نام معادل انسانی و تنها تفاوت واقعی را نشان می‌دهد. مدلی شماتیک برای یادگیری، نه یک مرجع بالینی.
purpose.pl: Zootomy to porównawczy atlas mięśni psa, kota i konia. Obróć zwierzę jednym palcem, dotknij mięśnia, aby przeczytać, co robi U TEGO GATUNKU, i zmieniaj gatunek za pomocą zakładek — wybór zostaje zapamiętany, ponieważ ten sam mięsień ma ten sam id we wszystkich trzech. Każda karta podaje też odpowiednik ludzki i jedną prawdziwą różnicę. Model schematyczny do nauki, nie referencja kliniczna.
purpose.uk: Zootomy — це порівняльний м'язовий атлас собаки, кота й коня. Обертайте тварину одним пальцем, торкайтеся м'яза, щоб прочитати, що він робить У ЦЬОГО ВИДУ, і перемикайте вид на вкладках — ваш вибір зберігається, оскільки той самий м'яз має той самий id у всіх трьох. Кожна картка також дає людський відповідник і одну справді відмінну рису. Схематична модель для навчання, не клінічний довідник.
purpose.nl: Zootomy is een vergelijkende spieratlas voor hond, kat en paard. Draai het dier met één vinger, tik op een spier om te lezen wat die BIJ DIE SOORT doet, en wissel van soort via de tabs — je keuze blijft behouden, omdat dezelfde spier bij alle drie hetzelfde id draagt. Elke kaart geeft ook de menselijke tegenhanger en het ene echt verschillende punt. Schematisch model, om te leren, geen klinische referentie.
purpose.sv: Zootomy är en jämförande muskelatlas för hund, katt och häst. Vrid djuret med ett finger, tryck på en muskel för att läsa vad den gör HOS DEN ARTEN, och byt art via flikarna — ditt val följer med, eftersom samma muskel har samma id hos alla tre. Varje kort ger också det mänskliga motsvarighetsnamnet och den enda verkligt annorlunda saken. Schematisk modell, för lärande, ingen klinisk referens.
purpose.cs: Zootomy je srovnávací svalový atlas pro psa, kočku a koně. Otočte zvíře jedním prstem, klepnutím na sval si přečtěte, co dělá U DANÉHO DRUHU, a přepínejte druh pomocí karet — váš výběr zůstává zachován, protože stejný sval nese stejné id u všech tří. Každá karta také uvádí lidský ekvivalent a jednu skutečně odlišnou vlastnost. Schematický model pro učení, nikoli klinický zdroj.
purpose.el: Το Zootomy είναι ένας συγκριτικός μυϊκός άτλαντας για σκύλο, γάτα και άλογο. Γυρίστε το ζώο με ένα δάχτυλο, πατήστε σε έναν μυ για να διαβάσετε τι κάνει ΣΕ ΑΥΤΟ ΤΟ ΕΙΔΟΣ, και αλλάξτε είδος από τις καρτέλες — η επιλογή σας σας ακολουθεί, επειδή ο ίδιος μυς φέρει το ίδιο id και στα τρία. Κάθε κάρτα δίνει επίσης το ανθρώπινο αντίστοιχο όνομα και το ένα πράγμα που είναι πραγματικά διαφορετικό. Σχηματικό μοντέλο, για εκμάθηση, όχι κλινική αναφορά.

model.title: Dog — muscles & skeleton
model.subtitle: Canis lupus familiaris · Selection carries across species: a muscle you pick here stays picked when you switch. Every muscle in this model is present in Dog.
model.disclaimer: Schematic comparative model — for learning, not a veterinary or clinical reference. Proportions and muscle paths are simplified to show topography and homology, not to measure anything.

parts.name: Skull
parts.info: The braincase and the long face in front of it. How far the face runs out ahead of the eye is one of the quickest ways to tell these three apart.

parts.name: Lower jaw (mandible)
parts.info: The lower jaw. Its rear corner is the lever arm the big chewing muscles pull on.

parts.name: Neck bones (cervical spine)
parts.info: Seven neck vertebrae — the same count in all three animals, and in you. Length, not number, is what makes a horse neck a horse neck.

parts.name: Chest spine (thoracic)
parts.info: The rib-bearing part of the backbone. Its tall upward spines at the front build the withers and give the neck and back muscles something to pull against.

parts.name: Loin spine (lumbar)
parts.info: The unsupported span between ribcage and pelvis. A cat flexes and extends it hugely when it bounds; a horse keeps it stiff and uses it to transmit drive from behind.

parts.name: Sacrum
parts.info: Fused vertebrae welded into the pelvis. This is where hindlimb thrust is handed to the spine.

parts.name: Tail bones (caudal)
parts.info: The tail is spine. It steers a running cat, balances and signals in a dog, and in a horse carries a long switch of hair.

parts.name: Breastbone (sternum)
parts.info: The floor of the chest. The ribs curve down to meet it, and the big chest muscles start here.

parts.name: Shoulder blade (scapula)
parts.info: A flat blade that is NOT hinged to the spine — it is held on by muscle alone and slides on the ribcage. That sliding is most of a quadruped's forelimb reach.

parts.name: Upper arm bone (humerus)
parts.info: Shoulder joint to elbow. It slopes backwards and downwards, so the elbow sits well behind and below the point of the shoulder.

parts.name: Forearm bones (radius & ulna)
parts.info: The forearm. Its point at the back — the olecranon — is the lever the triceps pulls to straighten the elbow.

parts.name: Wrist bones (carpus)
parts.info: The wrist. In a standing animal this is NOT the knee, however much it looks like one — it bends backwards, not forwards.

parts.name: Front cannon (metacarpus)
parts.info: The bones of the palm, stood on end. How long this column is, and how many bones are left in it, is the single biggest difference between these three legs.

parts.name: Front toes (digits)
parts.info: The fingers the animal actually stands on. Four bear weight in a dog and a cat; a horse has ground contact on one.

parts.name: Pelvis
parts.info: The bony basin bolted to the sacrum. Its front point (the hip bone you can feel) and its back point are the anchors for the whole hindquarter.

parts.name: Thigh bone (femur)
parts.info: Hip to stifle. In a standing quadruped it is angled forward and is largely buried inside the flank.

parts.name: Kneecap (patella)
parts.info: The kneecap, riding in the tendon of the big thigh muscle. In a horse it can be hooked over a ridge on the femur so the animal can stand asleep without holding the leg up.

parts.name: Shin bones (tibia & fibula)
parts.info: The shin. The second bone of the pair, the fibula, is a full bone in a cat and a dog and little more than a splint in a horse.

parts.name: Hock bones (tarsus)
parts.info: The ankle. The point sticking out at the back is the heel bone — the animal's Achilles lever.

parts.name: Rear cannon (metatarsus)
parts.info: The bones of the sole, stood on end — the hindlimb twin of the front cannon.

parts.name: Hind toes (digits)
parts.info: The toes the animal stands on behind — the hindlimb twin of the front ones, and the last link in the push-off.

parts.name: Ribs
parts.info: The bony cage the chest organs sit in, and the wall every trunk muscle pulls against. Rib count differs: dogs and cats carry thirteen pairs, a horse eighteen.

parts.name: Masseter
parts.info: Closes the jaw with force. The big, obvious cheek bulge.  Compare — Masseter — the same muscle you can feel bulge when you clench. Powerful but short-levered: a dog is built to grip and tear, so the jaw shuts fast rather than grinding.
parts.to: Outer face of the lower jaw

parts.name: Temporalis
parts.info: The other jaw-closer, pulling from the top of the skull. It fills the hollow behind the eye.  Compare — Temporalis — the muscle at your temple that moves when you chew. Big enough to build a ridge along the top of the skull in strong-jawed breeds — that crest is there purely to give this muscle more room.
parts.to: Coronoid process of the lower jaw

parts.name: Brachiocephalicus
parts.info: Runs head-to-arm down the side of the neck. Pulls the forelimb forward in the swing phase, and swings the head to the side when the limb is planted. The landmark that divides the upper neck from the lower one.  Compare — Roughly your sternocleidomastoid plus the front edge of your trapezius, fused into one strap because the collarbone that would separate them is missing or tiny. One continuous strap with only a faint tendinous line where a collarbone would be. It is the muscle you are feeling either side of a dog's neck.
parts.from: Back of the skull and the wing of the atlas
parts.to: Front of the upper arm bone

parts.name: Sternocephalicus
parts.info: Breastbone to head. Pulls the head and neck down and to the side.  Compare — The sternal half of your sternocleidomastoid. Slim and paired, meeting its partner low on the throat.
parts.to: Jaw and back of the skull

parts.name: Splenius
parts.info: Lifts the head and neck and holds them up. The main topline muscle of the neck.  Compare — Splenius capitis — the strap under the back of your neck. Moderate. A dog carries its head roughly level, so this works mostly to steady rather than to hold up.
parts.from: Withers and the ligament running forward from it
parts.to: Back of the skull and the first neck bones

parts.name: Omotransversarius
parts.info: Draws the shoulder blade forward, or bends the neck sideways when the limb is planted.  Compare — Closest match is levator scapulae — but yours cannot pull the shoulder blade forward the way this one does, because your collarbone anchors it. Clear flat band along the lower neck, easy to find under the skin.

parts.name: Trapezius
parts.info: A flat triangular sheet over the withers that lifts and swings the shoulder blade.  Compare — Trapezius — but yours reaches your collarbone, and theirs stops at the shoulder blade. Thin and broad; you are feeling it whenever you scratch a dog over the shoulder.
parts.from: Midline of the neck and withers

parts.name: Rhomboideus
parts.info: Pulls the top of the shoulder blade up and toward the midline. Lies underneath the trapezius.  Compare — Rhomboids, plus a neck portion you do not have. Well developed; helps hold the trunk up between the shoulder blades.
parts.to: Top edge of the shoulder blade

parts.name: Serratus ventralis
parts.info: THE SLING. The trunk has no bony joint with the forelimb at all; this fan of muscle from the ribs and neck to the inside of the shoulder blade is what the whole body actually hangs from.  Compare — Serratus anterior — same muscle, completely different job, because you hang your arm off a collarbone and they do not. Strong fan; takes the shock of every landing forelimb.
parts.from: Ribs and the lower neck bones
parts.to: Inner face of the shoulder blade

parts.name: Latissimus dorsi
parts.info: Draws the arm backwards and pulls the body forward over a planted forelimb. The big sheet over the side of the back.  Compare — Latissimus dorsi — the same broad back muscle, doing the same pull-the-arm-backwards job. Powerful — this is a lot of the drive in a dog dragging itself up over an obstacle.
parts.from: Fascia over the loin and the last ribs
parts.to: Inner face of the upper arm bone

parts.name: Longissimus dorsi
parts.info: The longest muscle in the body. Extends the back, and holds the spine rigid so hindlimb thrust reaches the front end instead of buckling the middle.  Compare — Erector spinae — the long columns either side of your backbone. Works with a fairly flexible back — a galloping dog flexes and extends its spine with every stride.

parts.name: Iliocostalis
parts.info: Lies just outside longissimus and bends the trunk sideways as well as extending it.  Compare — Iliocostalis — the outer column of your erector spinae. Contributes to the sideways whip of a turning dog.

parts.name: Superficial pectoral
parts.info: Pulls the forelimb toward the midline and stops it sliding out sideways. Forms the visible chest between the front legs.  Compare — The upper part of your pectoralis major. Gives a broad-chested dog its front. Divided into two clear bellies.
parts.to: Front of the upper arm bone

parts.name: Deep pectoral
parts.info: Pulls the trunk forward over a planted forelimb, and helps sling the chest between the shoulders.  Compare — The lower, sternal part of your pectoralis major. Substantial; contributes to the sling along with serratus.

parts.name: Rectus abdominis
parts.info: The straight belly strap. Curls the back, supports the abdomen, and helps with forced breathing.  Compare — Rectus abdominis — your "six-pack" strap, with the same cross-bands. Strong; part of the deep tuck-up behind the ribs.

parts.name: External abdominal oblique
parts.info: The big sheet covering the flank. Compresses the abdomen, twists the trunk, and holds the gut in.  Compare — External oblique — the same sheet down your flank. Covers most of the visible flank.
parts.to: Pelvis and the midline of the belly

parts.name: Cutaneous trunci
parts.info: A thin muscle sheet in the SKIN itself. Twitches the hide to shake off flies and dirt. Its reflex response is a routine nerve check.  Compare — No real human equivalent. The nearest leftovers in you are the small muscle under the skin of the palm and the sheet in your neck — you cannot twitch your back skin, and they can. Well developed over the trunk. The "panniculus" skin-twitch reflex is a standard part of a neurological exam.
parts.from: Deep fascia over the flank and armpit

parts.name: Supraspinatus
parts.info: Fills the front hollow of the shoulder blade. Extends the shoulder and, more importantly, stops it collapsing when the limb is loaded.  Compare — Supraspinatus — the top rotator-cuff muscle. Moderate; a stabiliser more than a mover.
parts.from: Front hollow of the shoulder blade

parts.name: Infraspinatus
parts.info: Fills the rear hollow of the shoulder blade, rotates the arm outward, and braces the joint from the side.  Compare — Infraspinatus — the rotator-cuff muscle behind your shoulder blade's ridge. Palpable behind the shoulder ridge; a common site of shoulder lameness.
parts.from: Rear hollow of the shoulder blade
parts.to: Outer side of the arm bone

parts.name: Deltoid
parts.info: Flexes the shoulder and swings the arm out to the side.  Compare — Deltoid — but yours wraps the whole shoulder because it also grips your collarbone. A clear two-part muscle over the point of the shoulder.
parts.from: Ridge of the shoulder blade and its rear border
parts.to: A bump partway down the arm bone

parts.name: Triceps brachii
parts.info: Straightens the elbow, and holds it straight against the animal's weight every moment it is standing. The big mass filling the angle between shoulder blade and arm.  Compare — Triceps — same three heads, same job. Bulky and obvious; the biggest muscle of the canine forelimb.
parts.from: Rear border of the shoulder blade and the arm bone

parts.name: Biceps brachii
parts.info: Bends the elbow and, with its long tendon over the front of the shoulder, stops the shoulder folding under load.  Compare — Biceps — but theirs cannot turn the palm up, because their forearm bones barely rotate. A straightforward working elbow flexor, with a normal fleshy belly along the front of the arm.

parts.name: Brachialis
parts.info: The pure elbow flexor, winding round the outside of the arm bone in a shallow groove.  Compare — Brachialis — same muscle, spiralling round the arm bone the same way. Distinct band lateral to the biceps.
parts.from: Back of the upper arm bone

parts.name: Teres major
parts.info: Works with latissimus to pull the arm backwards and inwards.  Compare — Teres major — same muscle, same partnership with latissimus. Clear strap on the inner shoulder.
parts.from: Rear border of the shoulder blade
parts.to: Inner face of the arm bone

parts.name: Extensor carpi radialis
parts.info: Straightens the wrist and carries the limb forward in the swing. The most prominent muscle on the front of the forearm.  Compare — Extensor carpi radialis — the muscle on the thumb side of your forearm that cocks your wrist back. Fleshy well down the forearm, and easy to feel tightening when the paw is lifted.
parts.from: Lower end of the arm bone

parts.name: Common digital extensor
parts.info: Straightens the toes so the foot clears the ground and lands flat.  Compare — Extensor digitorum — the tendons you can see fanning across the back of your hand. Fans into four tendons, one per weight-bearing toe.
parts.from: Lower end of the arm bone

parts.name: Deep digital flexor
parts.info: Curls the toes and supports the fetlock against the ground. Runs down the BACK of the leg.  Compare — Flexor digitorum profundus — the deep tendon that bends the end joint of your fingers. Fleshy for much of its length; flexes the toes for grip and digging.
parts.from: Elbow and the back of the forearm

parts.name: Flexor carpi ulnaris
parts.info: Bends the wrist backwards. Sits along the back edge of the forearm.  Compare — Flexor carpi ulnaris — the little-finger-side wrist flexor. Easy to palpate on the caudal forearm.

parts.name: Gluteus medius
parts.info: The main engine of the hindquarter: extends the hip and drives the body forward.  Compare — Gluteus medius — but in you it mostly steadies the pelvis when you stand on one leg, and in them it is a propulsion engine. Large; a sprinting dog is largely this muscle and the hamstrings.
parts.from: Wing of the pelvis and the loin
parts.to: The bump on top of the thigh bone

parts.name: Superficial gluteal
parts.info: Extends the hip and swings the limb out to the side.  Compare — Gluteus maximus — your biggest buttock muscle, which is far larger in you than in any of them because you stand upright. Small and superficial over the point of the hip.

parts.name: Tensor fasciae latae
parts.info: Tightens the sheet on the outside of the thigh and swings the limb forward.  Compare — Tensor fasciae latae — the same small muscle at the front of your hip, tightening the same band down the outside of the thigh. Forms the front edge of the flank triangle.

parts.name: Quadriceps femoris
parts.info: Straightens the stifle — the true knee — and flexes the hip. Fills the front of the thigh.  Compare — Quadriceps — same four heads, same kneecap tendon. Big; drives the extension phase of the stride.
parts.to: Kneecap and the top of the shin

parts.name: Biceps femoris
parts.info: The big muscle down the back and outside of the thigh. Extends the hip, and can either bend or straighten the stifle depending on which part pulls.  Compare — Biceps femoris — the outer hamstring. The obvious outline of a dog's upper hind leg.
parts.from: Sacrum and the point of the buttock
parts.to: Kneecap, shin and the heel tendon

parts.name: Semitendinosus
parts.info: Extends the hip and bends the stifle. Its rear border makes the clean vertical line at the back of the thigh.  Compare — Semitendinosus — the inner hamstring, with the same long tendon. Defines the back edge of the thigh.
parts.to: Inner shin and the heel tendon

parts.name: Semimembranosus
parts.info: Extends the hip and pulls the limb inward. Lies on the inside of the thigh, behind the others.  Compare — Semimembranosus — the deep inner hamstring. Forms much of the inner thigh, and is the mass you push aside to reach the femoral vessels.
parts.to: Inner side of the thigh bone and shin

parts.name: Sartorius
parts.info: A thin band down the front and inside of the thigh. Swings the limb forward and pulls it inward.  Compare — Sartorius — the long strap that runs diagonally across the front of your thigh. Two clear parts on the front of the thigh.

parts.name: Gracilis
parts.info: A broad thin sheet on the inside of the thigh that pulls the limb toward the midline.  Compare — Gracilis — the inner-thigh strap that pulls your legs together. Covers most of the inner thigh; the first sheet you meet approaching the femoral vessels.

parts.name: Gastrocnemius
parts.info: Straightens the hock and bends the stifle. Its tendon is the Achilles, and the animal's whole push-off runs through it.  Compare — Gastrocnemius — your calf muscle, ending in your Achilles tendon. Fleshy calf; a ruptured Achilles here drops the hock to the ground, which is unmistakable.
parts.from: Lower end of the thigh bone

parts.name: Superficial digital flexor
parts.info: Runs from the thigh bone, over the point of the hock, down to the toes. Flexes the toes and supports the fetlock.  Compare — Flexor digitorum superficialis — the tendon that bends the middle joint of your fingers and toes. Has a real muscle belly and works as a muscle.
parts.from: Lower end of the thigh bone

parts.name: Cranial tibial
parts.info: Bends the hock, lifting the foot clear of the ground in the swing phase.  Compare — Tibialis anterior — the muscle on the front of your shin that lifts your foot. Fleshy along most of the shin, and the muscle a dog uses to pick its paw up over an obstacle.

parts.name: Fibularis (peroneus) longus
parts.info: Bends the hock and rotates the foot outward. Lies on the outer side of the shin, alongside the second shin bone.  Compare — Fibularis (peroneus) longus — the muscle running down the outside of your calf behind the ankle bone. Present and functional, running with a complete fibula.
parts.from: Outer side of the top of the shin

parts.name: Skull
parts.info: The braincase and the long face in front of it. How far the face runs out ahead of the eye is one of the quickest ways to tell these three apart.

parts.name: Lower jaw (mandible)
parts.info: The lower jaw. Its rear corner is the lever arm the big chewing muscles pull on.

parts.name: Neck bones (cervical spine)
parts.info: Seven neck vertebrae — the same count in all three animals, and in you. Length, not number, is what makes a horse neck a horse neck.

parts.name: Chest spine (thoracic)
parts.info: The rib-bearing part of the backbone. Its tall upward spines at the front build the withers and give the neck and back muscles something to pull against.

parts.name: Loin spine (lumbar)
parts.info: The unsupported span between ribcage and pelvis. A cat flexes and extends it hugely when it bounds; a horse keeps it stiff and uses it to transmit drive from behind.

parts.name: Sacrum
parts.info: Fused vertebrae welded into the pelvis. This is where hindlimb thrust is handed to the spine.

parts.name: Tail bones (caudal)
parts.info: The tail is spine. It steers a running cat, balances and signals in a dog, and in a horse carries a long switch of hair.

parts.name: Breastbone (sternum)
parts.info: The floor of the chest. The ribs curve down to meet it, and the big chest muscles start here.

parts.name: Shoulder blade (scapula)
parts.info: A flat blade that is NOT hinged to the spine — it is held on by muscle alone and slides on the ribcage. That sliding is most of a quadruped's forelimb reach.

parts.name: Upper arm bone (humerus)
parts.info: Shoulder joint to elbow. It slopes backwards and downwards, so the elbow sits well behind and below the point of the shoulder.

parts.name: Forearm bones (radius & ulna)
parts.info: The forearm. Its point at the back — the olecranon — is the lever the triceps pulls to straighten the elbow.

parts.name: Wrist bones (carpus)
parts.info: The wrist. In a standing animal this is NOT the knee, however much it looks like one — it bends backwards, not forwards.

parts.name: Front cannon (metacarpus)
parts.info: The bones of the palm, stood on end. How long this column is, and how many bones are left in it, is the single biggest difference between these three legs.

parts.name: Front toes (digits)
parts.info: The fingers the animal actually stands on. Four bear weight in a dog and a cat; a horse has ground contact on one.

parts.name: Pelvis
parts.info: The bony basin bolted to the sacrum. Its front point (the hip bone you can feel) and its back point are the anchors for the whole hindquarter.

parts.name: Thigh bone (femur)
parts.info: Hip to stifle. In a standing quadruped it is angled forward and is largely buried inside the flank.

parts.name: Kneecap (patella)
parts.info: The kneecap, riding in the tendon of the big thigh muscle. In a horse it can be hooked over a ridge on the femur so the animal can stand asleep without holding the leg up.

parts.name: Shin bones (tibia & fibula)
parts.info: The shin. The second bone of the pair, the fibula, is a full bone in a cat and a dog and little more than a splint in a horse.

parts.name: Hock bones (tarsus)
parts.info: The ankle. The point sticking out at the back is the heel bone — the animal's Achilles lever.

parts.name: Rear cannon (metatarsus)
parts.info: The bones of the sole, stood on end — the hindlimb twin of the front cannon.

parts.name: Hind toes (digits)
parts.info: The toes the animal stands on behind — the hindlimb twin of the front ones, and the last link in the push-off.

parts.name: Collarbone (clavicle)
parts.info: A small floating collarbone, joined to the rest of the skeleton by muscle only. A cat has one; a dog has a vestigial nodule that does no work; a horse has none at all. This is why a cat can rotate and reach with its forelimb far more than the other two.
parts.from: Free in muscle near the point of the shoulder

parts.name: Ribs
parts.info: The bony cage the chest organs sit in, and the wall every trunk muscle pulls against. Rib count differs: dogs and cats carry thirteen pairs, a horse eighteen.

parts.name: Masseter
parts.info: Closes the jaw with force. The big, obvious cheek bulge.  Compare — Masseter — the same muscle you can feel bulge when you clench. Proportionally the largest of the three. A cat's whole skull is short, which turns the masseter into a very short, very strong lever for a killing bite.
parts.to: Outer face of the lower jaw

parts.name: Temporalis
parts.info: The other jaw-closer, pulling from the top of the skull. It fills the hollow behind the eye.  Compare — Temporalis — the muscle at your temple that moves when you chew. Very large for the head size, and the main reason a cat's skull looks domed between the ears.
parts.to: Coronoid process of the lower jaw

parts.name: Brachiocephalicus
parts.info: Runs head-to-arm down the side of the neck. Pulls the forelimb forward in the swing phase, and swings the head to the side when the limb is planted. The landmark that divides the upper neck from the lower one.  Compare — Roughly your sternocleidomastoid plus the front edge of your trapezius, fused into one strap because the collarbone that would separate them is missing or tiny. Split more clearly by the cat's small real collarbone, giving the shoulder more independent reach and rotation than a dog gets.
parts.from: Back of the skull and the wing of the atlas
parts.to: Front of the upper arm bone

parts.name: Sternocephalicus
parts.info: Breastbone to head. Pulls the head and neck down and to the side.  Compare — The sternal half of your sternocleidomastoid. Thin and easily missed; the cat leans on neck flexibility rather than pull here.
parts.to: Jaw and back of the skull

parts.name: Splenius
parts.info: Lifts the head and neck and holds them up. The main topline muscle of the neck.  Compare — Splenius capitis — the strap under the back of your neck. Light — a cat's head is small and its neck short.
parts.from: Withers and the ligament running forward from it
parts.to: Back of the skull and the first neck bones

parts.name: Omotransversarius
parts.info: Draws the shoulder blade forward, or bends the neck sideways when the limb is planted.  Compare — Closest match is levator scapulae — but yours cannot pull the shoulder blade forward the way this one does, because your collarbone anchors it. Prominent — part of how a stalking cat slides its shoulder blade so far forward.

parts.name: Trapezius
parts.info: A flat triangular sheet over the withers that lifts and swings the shoulder blade.  Compare — Trapezius — but yours reaches your collarbone, and theirs stops at the shoulder blade. Divided into distinct parts around the clavicle, which is part of the cat's extra shoulder freedom.
parts.from: Midline of the neck and withers

parts.name: Rhomboideus
parts.info: Pulls the top of the shoulder blade up and toward the midline. Lies underneath the trapezius.  Compare — Rhomboids, plus a neck portion you do not have. Long neck portion — it can hoist the shoulder blade above the line of the back, which is exactly what you see in a cat creeping forward.
parts.to: Top edge of the shoulder blade

parts.name: Serratus ventralis
parts.info: THE SLING. The trunk has no bony joint with the forelimb at all; this fan of muscle from the ribs and neck to the inside of the shoulder blade is what the whole body actually hangs from.  Compare — Serratus anterior — same muscle, completely different job, because you hang your arm off a collarbone and they do not. Elastic and mobile — it lets the trunk drop between the shoulder blades when a cat lands from a height.
parts.from: Ribs and the lower neck bones
parts.to: Inner face of the shoulder blade

parts.name: Latissimus dorsi
parts.info: Draws the arm backwards and pulls the body forward over a planted forelimb. The big sheet over the side of the back.  Compare — Latissimus dorsi — the same broad back muscle, doing the same pull-the-arm-backwards job. Very strong for the animal's size; a cat climbing uses it hard.
parts.from: Fascia over the loin and the last ribs
parts.to: Inner face of the upper arm bone

parts.name: Longissimus dorsi
parts.info: The longest muscle in the body. Extends the back, and holds the spine rigid so hindlimb thrust reaches the front end instead of buckling the middle.  Compare — Erector spinae — the long columns either side of your backbone. Extremely elastic. The cat's bound is largely this muscle and the loin unrolling.

parts.name: Iliocostalis
parts.info: Lies just outside longissimus and bends the trunk sideways as well as extending it.  Compare — Iliocostalis — the outer column of your erector spinae. Very active in the cat's side-to-side twist mid-leap.

parts.name: Superficial pectoral
parts.info: Pulls the forelimb toward the midline and stops it sliding out sideways. Forms the visible chest between the front legs.  Compare — The upper part of your pectoralis major. Slim, matching the cat's narrow chest.
parts.to: Front of the upper arm bone

parts.name: Deep pectoral
parts.info: Pulls the trunk forward over a planted forelimb, and helps sling the chest between the shoulders.  Compare — The lower, sternal part of your pectoralis major. Assists the cat in pulling itself up onto a ledge.

parts.name: Rectus abdominis
parts.info: The straight belly strap. Curls the back, supports the abdomen, and helps with forced breathing.  Compare — Rectus abdominis — your "six-pack" strap, with the same cross-bands. Very strong relative to size — a cat pulling its hind legs up under itself mid-jump is using this hard.

parts.name: External abdominal oblique
parts.info: The big sheet covering the flank. Compresses the abdomen, twists the trunk, and holds the gut in.  Compare — External oblique — the same sheet down your flank. Thin but very extensible — a cat can fold almost double.
parts.to: Pelvis and the midline of the belly

parts.name: Cutaneous trunci
parts.info: A thin muscle sheet in the SKIN itself. Twitches the hide to shake off flies and dirt. Its reflex response is a routine nerve check.  Compare — No real human equivalent. The nearest leftovers in you are the small muscle under the skin of the palm and the sheet in your neck — you cannot twitch your back skin, and they can. Present and brisk; also part of the classic rippling-skin response.
parts.from: Deep fascia over the flank and armpit

parts.name: Supraspinatus
parts.info: Fills the front hollow of the shoulder blade. Extends the shoulder and, more importantly, stops it collapsing when the limb is loaded.  Compare — Supraspinatus — the top rotator-cuff muscle. Slim — the cat wants shoulder mobility, not rigidity.
parts.from: Front hollow of the shoulder blade

parts.name: Infraspinatus
parts.info: Fills the rear hollow of the shoulder blade, rotates the arm outward, and braces the joint from the side.  Compare — Infraspinatus — the rotator-cuff muscle behind your shoulder blade's ridge. Fine and very mobile — the cat trades bracing strength here for a shoulder that can rotate and reach.
parts.from: Rear hollow of the shoulder blade
parts.to: Outer side of the arm bone

parts.name: Deltoid
parts.info: Flexes the shoulder and swings the arm out to the side.  Compare — Deltoid — but yours wraps the whole shoulder because it also grips your collarbone. Relatively large, and with the clavicle it gives the cat genuine sideways reach — a cat can bat sideways, a horse cannot.
parts.from: Ridge of the shoulder blade and its rear border
parts.to: A bump partway down the arm bone

parts.name: Triceps brachii
parts.info: Straightens the elbow, and holds it straight against the animal's weight every moment it is standing. The big mass filling the angle between shoulder blade and arm.  Compare — Triceps — same three heads, same job. Strong and fast — this is the push in a cat's pounce.
parts.from: Rear border of the shoulder blade and the arm bone

parts.name: Biceps brachii
parts.info: Bends the elbow and, with its long tendon over the front of the shoulder, stops the shoulder folding under load.  Compare — Biceps — but theirs cannot turn the palm up, because their forearm bones barely rotate. Retains real rotation — a cat can turn its paw to grip and to wash its face, which a horse can never do.

parts.name: Brachialis
parts.info: The pure elbow flexor, winding round the outside of the arm bone in a shallow groove.  Compare — Brachialis — same muscle, spiralling round the arm bone the same way. Well developed; a cat pulls with its forelimbs constantly.
parts.from: Back of the upper arm bone

parts.name: Teres major
parts.info: Works with latissimus to pull the arm backwards and inwards.  Compare — Teres major — same muscle, same partnership with latissimus. Strong; part of the pull a climbing cat generates.
parts.from: Rear border of the shoulder blade
parts.to: Inner face of the arm bone

parts.name: Extensor carpi radialis
parts.info: Straightens the wrist and carries the limb forward in the swing. The most prominent muscle on the front of the forearm.  Compare — Extensor carpi radialis — the muscle on the thumb side of your forearm that cocks your wrist back. Fleshy and mobile, matching the cat's flexible wrist.
parts.from: Lower end of the arm bone

parts.name: Common digital extensor
parts.info: Straightens the toes so the foot clears the ground and lands flat.  Compare — Extensor digitorum — the tendons you can see fanning across the back of your hand. Four tendons, and the cat can spread its toes and put out its claws independently.
parts.from: Lower end of the arm bone

parts.name: Deep digital flexor
parts.info: Curls the toes and supports the fetlock against the ground. Runs down the BACK of the leg.  Compare — Flexor digitorum profundus — the deep tendon that bends the end joint of your fingers. Works with the claw mechanism — the same pull that flexes the toe protrudes the claw.
parts.from: Elbow and the back of the forearm

parts.name: Flexor carpi ulnaris
parts.info: Bends the wrist backwards. Sits along the back edge of the forearm.  Compare — Flexor carpi ulnaris — the little-finger-side wrist flexor. Prominent; a cat flexes its wrist through a wide range.

parts.name: Gluteus medius
parts.info: The main engine of the hindquarter: extends the hip and drives the body forward.  Compare — Gluteus medius — but in you it mostly steadies the pelvis when you stand on one leg, and in them it is a propulsion engine. Fast and powerful for its size — the launch of a vertical jump.
parts.from: Wing of the pelvis and the loin
parts.to: The bump on top of the thigh bone

parts.name: Superficial gluteal
parts.info: Extends the hip and swings the limb out to the side.  Compare — Gluteus maximus — your biggest buttock muscle, which is far larger in you than in any of them because you stand upright. Small — the cat's power sits deeper.

parts.name: Tensor fasciae latae
parts.info: Tightens the sheet on the outside of the thigh and swings the limb forward.  Compare — Tensor fasciae latae — the same small muscle at the front of your hip, tightening the same band down the outside of the thigh. Slim — a cat swings its hind limb forward with the hip and spine rather than with this small muscle.

parts.name: Quadriceps femoris
parts.info: Straightens the stifle — the true knee — and flexes the hip. Fills the front of the thigh.  Compare — Quadriceps — same four heads, same kneecap tendon. Explosive rather than enduring.
parts.to: Kneecap and the top of the shin

parts.name: Biceps femoris
parts.info: The big muscle down the back and outside of the thigh. Extends the hip, and can either bend or straighten the stifle depending on which part pulls.  Compare — Biceps femoris — the outer hamstring. Long and elastic; part of the cat's spring.
parts.from: Sacrum and the point of the buttock
parts.to: Kneecap, shin and the heel tendon

parts.name: Semitendinosus
parts.info: Extends the hip and bends the stifle. Its rear border makes the clean vertical line at the back of the thigh.  Compare — Semitendinosus — the inner hamstring, with the same long tendon. Long-bellied, strongly flexes the knee for the tuck of a jump.
parts.to: Inner shin and the heel tendon

parts.name: Semimembranosus
parts.info: Extends the hip and pulls the limb inward. Lies on the inside of the thigh, behind the others.  Compare — Semimembranosus — the deep inner hamstring. Slim and deep, tucked behind the other hamstrings on the inside of the thigh.
parts.to: Inner side of the thigh bone and shin

parts.name: Sartorius
parts.info: A thin band down the front and inside of the thigh. Swings the limb forward and pulls it inward.  Compare — Sartorius — the long strap that runs diagonally across the front of your thigh. Broad and flat, covering much of the inner thigh.

parts.name: Gracilis
parts.info: A broad thin sheet on the inside of the thigh that pulls the limb toward the midline.  Compare — Gracilis — the inner-thigh strap that pulls your legs together. Broad and thin, sheeting most of the inner thigh under very loose skin.

parts.name: Gastrocnemius
parts.info: Straightens the hock and bends the stifle. Its tendon is the Achilles, and the animal's whole push-off runs through it.  Compare — Gastrocnemius — your calf muscle, ending in your Achilles tendon. Powerful and quick — the main muscle behind a cat's vertical leap.
parts.from: Lower end of the thigh bone

parts.name: Superficial digital flexor
parts.info: Runs from the thigh bone, over the point of the hock, down to the toes. Flexes the toes and supports the fetlock.  Compare — Flexor digitorum superficialis — the tendon that bends the middle joint of your fingers and toes. Fleshy and mobile, and it works with the claw mechanism when the cat grips with a hind foot.
parts.from: Lower end of the thigh bone

parts.name: Cranial tibial
parts.info: Bends the hock, lifting the foot clear of the ground in the swing phase.  Compare — Tibialis anterior — the muscle on the front of your shin that lifts your foot. Well developed; the cat picks its feet up precisely.

parts.name: Fibularis (peroneus) longus
parts.info: Bends the hock and rotates the foot outward. Lies on the outer side of the shin, alongside the second shin bone.  Compare — Fibularis (peroneus) longus — the muscle running down the outside of your calf behind the ankle bone. Present and well developed — part of how a cat turns its hind foot to grip and to climb down head-first.
parts.from: Outer side of the top of the shin

Blends with the brachiocephalicus and is harder to separate as a distinct muscle on the standing animal.

parts.name: Trapezius
parts.info: A flat triangular sheet over the withers that lifts and swings the shoulder blade.  Compare — Trapezius — but yours reaches your collarbone, and theirs stops at the shoulder blade. Thin over a very large area, and it lies exactly where a saddle sits — so soreness here is a saddle-fit question before it is anything else.
parts.from: Midline of the neck and withers

parts.name: Rhomboideus
parts.info: Pulls the top of the shoulder blade up and toward the midline. Lies underneath the trapezius.  Compare — Rhomboids, plus a neck portion you do not have. Thick and short, working with serratus ventralis to keep a half-tonne trunk hanging between the blades.
parts.to: Top edge of the shoulder blade

parts.name: Serratus ventralis
parts.info: THE SLING. The trunk has no bony joint with the forelimb at all; this fan of muscle from the ribs and neck to the inside of the shoulder blade is what the whole body actually hangs from.  Compare — Serratus anterior — same muscle, completely different job, because you hang your arm off a collarbone and they do not. The classic example of the thoracic sling, and one of the most important structures in the horse: it carries roughly sixty per cent of the animal's weight and is why a horse has no collarbone to shatter. Fatigue or damage here shows as a trunk that has sunk between the shoulder blades.
parts.from: Ribs and the lower neck bones
parts.to: Inner face of the shoulder blade

parts.name: Latissimus dorsi
parts.info: Draws the arm backwards and pulls the body forward over a planted forelimb. The big sheet over the side of the back.  Compare — Latissimus dorsi — the same broad back muscle, doing the same pull-the-arm-backwards job. Broad and flat, and it lies under the back of the saddle. Its rear border is the usual site for an intramuscular injection high on the neck's counterpart at the rear.
parts.from: Fascia over the loin and the last ribs
parts.to: Inner face of the upper arm bone

parts.name: Longissimus dorsi
parts.info: The longest muscle in the body. Extends the back, and holds the spine rigid so hindlimb thrust reaches the front end instead of buckling the middle.  Compare — Erector spinae — the long columns either side of your backbone. The horse's back is built to stay STIFF, and this is the muscle that keeps it that way. It sits directly under the saddle, so back pain in a ridden horse is a longissimus question until proven otherwise.

parts.name: Iliocostalis
parts.info: Lies just outside longissimus and bends the trunk sideways as well as extending it.  Compare — Iliocostalis — the outer column of your erector spinae. Present but overshadowed by longissimus; a horse deliberately limits sideways bend through the trunk.

parts.name: Superficial pectoral
parts.info: Pulls the forelimb toward the midline and stops it sliding out sideways. Forms the visible chest between the front legs.  Compare — The upper part of your pectoralis major. Builds the muscular V you see between a horse's front legs from in front.
parts.to: Front of the upper arm bone

parts.name: Deep pectoral
parts.info: Pulls the trunk forward over a planted forelimb, and helps sling the chest between the shoulders.  Compare — The lower, sternal part of your pectoralis major. Large. Its lower edge is a landmark for the girth line, and girth galls sit exactly over it.

parts.name: Rectus abdominis
parts.info: The straight belly strap. Curls the back, supports the abdomen, and helps with forced breathing.  Compare — Rectus abdominis — your "six-pack" strap, with the same cross-bands. Long and important for foaling and for supporting a very heavy gut. A dropped, pendulous belly in an older horse is this muscle and its sheath giving way.

parts.name: External abdominal oblique
parts.info: The big sheet covering the flank. Compresses the abdomen, twists the trunk, and holds the gut in.  Compare — External oblique — the same sheet down your flank. Broad, and its lower edge and the "flank fold" are standard landmarks. Colic pain shows up as guarding here.
parts.to: Pelvis and the midline of the belly

parts.name: Cutaneous trunci
parts.info: A thin muscle sheet in the SKIN itself. Twitches the hide to shake off flies and dirt. Its reflex response is a routine nerve check.  Compare — No real human equivalent. The nearest leftovers in you are the small muscle under the skin of the palm and the sheet in your neck — you cannot twitch your back skin, and they can. Very well developed — this is the muscle doing the fly-shudder along a horse's side, and its reflex maps the nerve supply of the trunk neatly.
parts.from: Deep fascia over the flank and armpit

parts.name: Supraspinatus
parts.info: Fills the front hollow of the shoulder blade. Extends the shoulder and, more importantly, stops it collapsing when the limb is loaded.  Compare — Supraspinatus — the top rotator-cuff muscle. Thick and, with infraspinatus, effectively replaces a shoulder joint capsule strong enough to hold half a tonne. In a horse this muscle IS the shoulder ligament.
parts.from: Front hollow of the shoulder blade

parts.name: Infraspinatus
parts.info: Fills the rear hollow of the shoulder blade, rotates the arm outward, and braces the joint from the side.  Compare — Infraspinatus — the rotator-cuff muscle behind your shoulder blade's ridge. Very strong; acts as the lateral collateral ligament of the shoulder, which is why an infraspinatus problem reads as instability rather than simple soreness.
parts.from: Rear hollow of the shoulder blade
parts.to: Outer side of the arm bone

parts.name: Deltoid
parts.info: Flexes the shoulder and swings the arm out to the side.  Compare — Deltoid — but yours wraps the whole shoulder because it also grips your collarbone. Comparatively small. A horse's forelimb swings almost purely forwards and backwards, so a muscle for sideways movement has little to do.
parts.from: Ridge of the shoulder blade and its rear border
parts.to: A bump partway down the arm bone

parts.name: Triceps brachii
parts.info: Straightens the elbow, and holds it straight against the animal's weight every moment it is standing. The big mass filling the angle between shoulder blade and arm.  Compare — Triceps — same three heads, same job. Massive. It works with the shoulder muscles as part of the standing mechanism that lets a horse doze on its feet with almost no muscular effort.
parts.from: Rear border of the shoulder blade and the arm bone

parts.name: Biceps brachii
parts.info: Bends the elbow and, with its long tendon over the front of the shoulder, stops the shoulder folding under load.  Compare — Biceps — but theirs cannot turn the palm up, because their forearm bones barely rotate. Mostly TENDON rather than muscle, and part of the stay apparatus: a fibrous band runs straight through it so the shoulder and elbow can be locked open without muscular work.

parts.name: Brachialis
parts.info: The pure elbow flexor, winding round the outside of the arm bone in a shallow groove.  Compare — Brachialis — same muscle, spiralling round the arm bone the same way. Present but modest — flexing the elbow is not a big part of what a horse leg does.
parts.from: Back of the upper arm bone

parts.name: Teres major
parts.info: Works with latissimus to pull the arm backwards and inwards.  Compare — Teres major — same muscle, same partnership with latissimus. Present and functional but hidden deep against the chest wall.
parts.from: Rear border of the shoulder blade
parts.to: Inner face of the arm bone

parts.name: Extensor carpi radialis
parts.info: Straightens the wrist and carries the limb forward in the swing. The most prominent muscle on the front of the forearm.  Compare — Extensor carpi radialis — the muscle on the thumb side of your forearm that cocks your wrist back. Becomes tendon high up and runs as a cord straight down the front of the cannon — one of the cords you can feel and follow on a standing horse.
parts.from: Lower end of the arm bone

parts.name: Common digital extensor
parts.info: Straightens the toes so the foot clears the ground and lands flat.  Compare — Extensor digitorum — the tendons you can see fanning across the back of your hand. ONE tendon to ONE toe. Everything that used to serve four digits now serves a single hoof — which is why a single extensor injury in a horse is a whole-limb problem.
parts.from: Lower end of the arm bone

parts.name: Deep digital flexor
parts.info: Curls the toes and supports the fetlock against the ground. Runs down the BACK of the leg.  Compare — Flexor digitorum profundus — the deep tendon that bends the end joint of your fingers. The cord down the back of the cannon, held in check by a ligament so it can support the fetlock without muscular effort. This tendon and its check ligament are among the most commonly injured structures in a performance horse.
parts.from: Elbow and the back of the forearm

parts.name: Flexor carpi ulnaris
parts.info: Bends the wrist backwards. Sits along the back edge of the forearm.  Compare — Flexor carpi ulnaris — the little-finger-side wrist flexor. Short-bellied with a long tendon, in keeping with the horse's pattern of putting muscle high and cord low.

parts.name: Gluteus medius
parts.info: The main engine of the hindquarter: extends the hip and drives the body forward.  Compare — Gluteus medius — but in you it mostly steadies the pelvis when you stand on one leg, and in them it is a propulsion engine. Enormous, and it runs FORWARD over the loin well past the pelvis, which no human gluteal does. This forward extension is why a horse's croup is muscled all the way to the back of the saddle.
parts.from: Wing of the pelvis and the loin
parts.to: The bump on top of the thigh bone

parts.name: Superficial gluteal
parts.info: Extends the hip and swings the limb out to the side.  Compare — Gluteus maximus — your biggest buttock muscle, which is far larger in you than in any of them because you stand upright. Fused with a strip running down to the thigh, forming one continuous band. The rounded outline of a horse's rump is this muscle over gluteus medius.

parts.name: Tensor fasciae latae
parts.info: Tightens the sheet on the outside of the thigh and swings the limb forward.  Compare — Tensor fasciae latae — the same small muscle at the front of your hip, tightening the same band down the outside of the thigh. Prominent, and its front border is a clear landmark on the standing horse — the visible fold in front of the thigh.

parts.name: Quadriceps femoris
parts.info: Straightens the stifle — the true knee — and flexes the hip. Fills the front of the thigh.  Compare — Quadriceps — same four heads, same kneecap tendon. Very large, and part of the stay apparatus: it can hitch the kneecap over a ridge on the thigh bone so the hind limb locks straight and the horse can sleep standing. A stifle that will not unlock is a real clinical presentation.
parts.to: Kneecap and the top of the shin

parts.name: Biceps femoris
parts.info: The big muscle down the back and outside of the thigh. Extends the hip, and can either bend or straighten the stifle depending on which part pulls.  Compare — Biceps femoris — the outer hamstring. Huge, and reaches much further forward onto the sacrum than a human hamstring does. The shape of a horse's thigh from behind is this muscle and semitendinosus side by side.
parts.from: Sacrum and the point of the buttock
parts.to: Kneecap, shin and the heel tendon

parts.name: Semitendinosus
parts.info: Extends the hip and bends the stifle. Its rear border makes the clean vertical line at the back of the thigh.  Compare — Semitendinosus — the inner hamstring, with the same long tendon. Its back border is the visible edge of the hindquarter seen from the side, and the gap between it and biceps femoris is a standard injection site.
parts.to: Inner shin and the heel tendon

parts.name: Semimembranosus
parts.info: Extends the hip and pulls the limb inward. Lies on the inside of the thigh, behind the others.  Compare — Semimembranosus — the deep inner hamstring. Thick; part of the mass you feel on the inside of a horse's thigh.
parts.to: Inner side of the thigh bone and shin

parts.name: Sartorius
parts.info: A thin band down the front and inside of the thigh. Swings the limb forward and pulls it inward.  Compare — Sartorius — the long strap that runs diagonally across the front of your thigh. Thin, and it helps roof the passage where the big vessels enter the hind limb — a landmark rather than a mover.

parts.name: Gracilis
parts.info: A broad thin sheet on the inside of the thigh that pulls the limb toward the midline.  Compare — Gracilis — the inner-thigh strap that pulls your legs together. Wide; the inside of a horse's thigh is largely gracilis over semimembranosus.

parts.name: Gastrocnemius
parts.info: Straightens the hock and bends the stifle. Its tendon is the Achilles, and the animal's whole push-off runs through it.  Compare — Gastrocnemius — your calf muscle, ending in your Achilles tendon. Muscular high up and tendon almost all the way down, and it is a working part of the RECIPROCAL apparatus: hock and stifle in a horse are mechanically chained, so one cannot bend without the other. That chain is what lets a horse rest a hind leg while standing.
parts.from: Lower end of the thigh bone

parts.name: Superficial digital flexor
parts.info: Runs from the thigh bone, over the point of the hock, down to the toes. Flexes the toes and supports the fetlock.  Compare — Flexor digitorum superficialis — the tendon that bends the middle joint of your fingers and toes. Almost entirely TENDINOUS in the hind limb, and it is the second half of the reciprocal apparatus with gastrocnemius. In the FRONT limb its counterpart is the most commonly strained tendon in racing and jumping.
parts.from: Lower end of the thigh bone

parts.name: Cranial tibial
parts.info: Bends the hock, lifting the foot clear of the ground in the swing phase.  Compare — Tibialis anterior — the muscle on the front of your shin that lifts your foot. Its tendon splits and one branch, the peroneus tertius, is a pure fibrous cord that mechanically ties hock to stifle. A torn cord shows up as the hock extending while the stifle stays bent — impossible in a sound horse.

value.en: Every muscle here carries the SAME id in all three species, so a pick made on the dog is still your pick on the horse. Search a human muscle name to find the animal one, see which of the three actually has it, and read what is different in each.
value.ko: 여기 모든 근육은 세 종 모두에서 같은 id를 가지므로, 개에서 고른 것이 말에서도 그대로 선택 상태가 됩니다. 인간 근육 이름을 검색해서 해당 동물 근육을 찾고, 셋 중 실제로 어느 동물에 있는지 확인하고, 각각 무엇이 다른지 읽어보세요.
value.zh: 这里的每块肌肉在三个物种中都使用同一个id，因此在狗身上选中的肌肉，在马身上依然是你的选择。搜索人类肌肉名称即可找到对应的动物肌肉，查看三者中哪些真正拥有它，并阅读各自的不同之处。
value.hi: यहाँ हर मांसपेशी तीनों प्रजातियों में एक ही id रखती है, इसलिए कुत्ते पर किया गया चयन घोड़े पर भी वही रहता है। मानव मांसपेशी का नाम खोजें ताकि पशु वाली मिल जाए, देखें कि तीनों में से किसमें वह वास्तव में है, और हर एक में क्या अलग है यह पढ़ें.
value.es: Cada músculo aquí lleva el MISMO id en las tres especies, así que una selección hecha en el perro sigue siendo tu selección en el caballo. Busca un nombre de músculo humano para encontrar el animal, mira cuál de los tres lo tiene realmente, y lee qué es diferente en cada uno.
value.fr: Chaque muscle porte ici le MÊME id dans les trois espèces, donc une sélection faite sur le chien reste votre sélection sur le cheval. Recherchez un nom de muscle humain pour trouver l'équivalent animal, voyez lequel des trois le possède réellement, et lisez ce qui diffère dans chacun.
value.ar: تحمل كل عضلة هنا نفس المعرف في الأنواع الثلاثة، لذا يبقى الاختيار الذي تم على الكلب هو اختيارك على الحصان. ابحث عن اسم عضلة بشرية للعثور على العضلة الحيوانية المقابلة، وشاهد أي الأنواع الثلاثة يمتلكها فعليًا، واقرأ ما يختلف في كل منها.
value.pt: Cada músculo aqui carrega o MESMO id nas três espécies, então uma seleção feita no cão continua sendo sua seleção no cavalo. Pesquise um nome de músculo humano para encontrar o do animal, veja qual dos três realmente o possui, e leia o que é diferente em cada um.
value.ru: Каждая мышца здесь несёт ОДИНАКОВЫЙ id у всех трёх видов, поэтому выбор, сделанный на собаке, остаётся вашим выбором и на лошади. Найдите название мышцы человека, чтобы отыскать её у животного, посмотрите, у кого из трёх она действительно есть, и прочитайте, чем каждая отличается.
value.de: Jeder Muskel hier trägt bei allen drei Arten dieselbe id, sodass eine beim Hund getroffene Auswahl auch beim Pferd erhalten bleibt. Sucht nach einem menschlichen Muskelnamen, um den tierischen zu finden, seht, welche der drei Arten ihn tatsächlich hat, und lest, was bei jeder anders ist.
value.ja: ここでのすべての筋肉は3種で同じidを持つため、犬で選んだものは馬でも同じ選択として引き継がれます。ヒトの筋肉名を検索して該当する動物の筋肉を見つけ、実際に3種のうちどれが持っているかを確認し、それぞれの違いを読んでみましょう。
value.tr: Buradaki her kas üç türde de AYNI id'yi taşır, bu yüzden köpekte yapılan bir seçim atta da seçiminiz olarak kalır. Hayvan karşılığını bulmak için bir insan kas adı arayın, üçünden hangisinde gerçekten bulunduğunu görün ve her birinde neyin farklı olduğunu okuyun.
value.vi: Mỗi cơ ở đây mang CÙNG một id ở cả ba loài, vì vậy lựa chọn trên chó vẫn là lựa chọn của bạn trên ngựa. Tìm kiếm tên cơ ở người để tìm cơ tương ứng ở động vật, xem loài nào trong ba loài thực sự có nó, và đọc điểm khác biệt ở mỗi loài.
value.it: Ogni muscolo qui porta lo STESSO id in tutte e tre le specie, quindi una scelta fatta sul cane resta la tua scelta anche sul cavallo. Cerca un nome di muscolo umano per trovare quello animale, vedi quale delle tre specie lo possiede realmente, e leggi cosa è diverso in ciascuna.
value.fa: هر عضله اینجا در هر سه گونه همان شناسه را دارد، بنابراین انتخابی که روی سگ انجام می‌دهید روی اسب هم همان انتخاب باقی می‌ماند. یک نام عضله انسانی جستجو کنید تا معادل حیوانی آن را بیابید، ببینید کدام‌یک از سه گونه واقعاً آن را دارد، و بخوانید در هرکدام چه تفاوتی دارد.
value.pl: Każdy mięsień tutaj ma TEN SAM id we wszystkich trzech gatunkach, więc wybór dokonany na psie pozostaje twoim wyborem na koniu. Wyszukaj ludzką nazwę mięśnia, aby znaleźć zwierzęcy odpowiednik, zobacz, który z trzech gatunków rzeczywiście go ma, i przeczytaj, co jest różne w każdym.
value.uk: Кожен м'яз тут має ОДНАКОВИЙ id у всіх трьох видів, тож вибір, зроблений на собаці, залишається вашим вибором і на коні. Знайдіть людську назву м'яза, щоб знайти тваринний відповідник, подивіться, у кого з трьох він справді є, і прочитайте, що відрізняється у кожного.
value.nl: Elke spier hier draagt hetzelfde id bij alle drie de soorten, dus een keuze gemaakt bij de hond blijft je keuze bij het paard. Zoek een menselijke spiernaam om de dierlijke tegenhanger te vinden, zie welke van de drie hem daadwerkelijk heeft, en lees wat er bij elk anders is.
value.sv: Varje muskel här har SAMMA id hos alla tre arterna, så ett val gjort på hunden förblir ditt val på hästen. Sök på ett mänskligt muskelnamn för att hitta djurets, se vilken av de tre som faktiskt har den, och läs vad som skiljer sig hos var och en.
value.cs: Každý sval zde nese STEJNÉ id u všech tří druhů, takže výběr provedený u psa zůstává vaším výběrem i u koně. Vyhledejte lidský název svalu, abyste našli ten zvířecí, zjistěte, který ze tří jej skutečně má, a přečtěte si, co je u každého jiné.
value.el: Κάθε μυς εδώ φέρει το ΙΔΙΟ id και στα τρία είδη, οπότε μια επιλογή στον σκύλο παραμένει η επιλογή σας και στο άλογο. Αναζητήστε ένα ανθρώπινο όνομα μυός για να βρείτε το αντίστοιχο ζωικό, δείτε ποιο από τα τρία το έχει πράγματι, και διαβάστε τι διαφέρει σε καθένα.

value.en: Schematic comparative model — for learning, not a veterinary or clinical reference. Proportions and muscle paths are simplified to show topography and homology, not to measure anything.

value.hi: यह एक स्कीमैटिक तुलनात्मक मॉडल है — सीखने के लिए, न कि पशु चिकित्सा या नैदानिक संदर्भ के लिए। अनुपात और मांसपेशी पथ स्थलाकृति और समजातता दिखाने के लिए सरल किए गए हैं, कुछ मापने के लिए नहीं।
value.es: Modelo comparativo esquemático — para aprender, no una referencia veterinaria o clínica. Las proporciones y trayectos musculares están simplificados para mostrar topografía y homología, no para medir nada.
value.fr: Modèle comparatif schématique — pour apprendre, pas une référence vétérinaire ou clinique. Les proportions et trajets musculaires sont simplifiés pour montrer la topographie et l'homologie, pas pour mesurer quoi que ce soit.
value.ar: نموذج مقارن تخطيطي — للتعلم فقط، وليس مرجعًا بيطريًا أو سريريًا. النسب ومسارات العضلات مبسّطة لإظهار الموضع والتماثل، لا لقياس أي شيء.
value.pt: Modelo comparativo esquemático — para aprendizado, não uma referência veterinária ou clínica. Proporções e trajetos musculares são simplificados para mostrar topografia e homologia, não para medir nada.
value.ru: Схематичная сравнительная модель — для обучения, не ветеринарный или клинический справочник. Пропорции и ход мышц упрощены, чтобы показать топографию и гомологию, а не для измерений.
value.de: Schematisches Vergleichsmodell — zum Lernen, kein tierärztliches oder klinisches Nachschlagewerk. Proportionen und Muskelverläufe sind vereinfacht, um Topografie und Homologie zu zeigen, nicht um irgendetwas zu vermessen.
value.ja: 学習用の模式的比較モデルであり、獣医学的・臨床的な参考資料ではありません。比率と筋肉の走行は、位置関係と相同性を示すために簡略化されており、何かを計測するためのものではありません。
value.tr: Şematik karşılaştırmalı model — öğrenim için, veterinerlik veya klinik referans değildir. Oranlar ve kas yolları, topografya ve homolojiyi göstermek için basitleştirilmiştir, herhangi bir şeyi ölçmek için değildir.
value.vi: Mô hình so sánh dạng sơ đồ — dùng để học, không phải tài liệu tham khảo thú y hay lâm sàng. Tỷ lệ và đường đi của cơ được đơn giản hóa để thể hiện vị trí và tính tương đồng, không nhằm mục đích đo lường.
value.it: Modello comparativo schematico — per l'apprendimento, non un riferimento veterinario o clinico. Proporzioni e decorsi muscolari sono semplificati per mostrare topografia e omologia, non per misurare alcunché.
value.fa: مدل مقایسه‌ای شماتیک — برای یادگیری، نه مرجع دامپزشکی یا بالینی. نسبت‌ها و مسیرهای عضلانی برای نشان دادن موقعیت و همولوژی ساده‌سازی شده‌اند، نه برای اندازه‌گیری چیزی.
value.pl: Schematyczny model porównawczy — do nauki, nie referencja weterynaryjna ani kliniczna. Proporcje i przebiegi mięśni są uproszczone, aby pokazać topografię i homologię, a nie do pomiarów.
value.uk: Схематична порівняльна модель — для навчання, не ветеринарний чи клінічний довідник. Пропорції та хід м'язів спрощені, щоб показати топографію та гомологію, а не для вимірювань.
value.nl: Schematisch vergelijkend model — om te leren, geen diergeneeskundige of klinische referentie. Verhoudingen en spierverlopen zijn vereenvoudigd om topografie en homologie te tonen, niet om iets te meten.
value.sv: Schematisk jämförande modell — för lärande, ingen veterinärmedicinsk eller klinisk referens. Proportioner och muskelbanor är förenklade för att visa topografi och homologi, inte för att mäta något.
value.cs: Schematický srovnávací model — pro učení, nikoli veterinární nebo klinický zdroj. Proporce a průběhy svalů jsou zjednodušené, aby ukázaly topografii a homologii, nikoli aby něco měřily.
value.el: Σχηματικό συγκριτικό μοντέλο — για εκμάθηση, όχι κτηνιατρική ή κλινική αναφορά. Οι αναλογίες και οι μυϊκές διαδρομές είναι απλοποιημένες για να δείξουν τοπογραφία και ομολογία, όχι για μέτρηση.
